groups.title: Oral Solution (A65401ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of functional asthenia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 sachet (1 g) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, diluted in water. Children aged 6 years and older: take 1 sachet (1 g) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, diluted in water. Do not take it for 4 weeks or more.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a young child under 6 years of age, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, consult a pharmacist.

Rarely, mild gastrointestinal disturbance and the like may occur at the start of treatment.

summaryTable.What it is for: Adjunctive treatment of functional asthenia

groups.title: Tablet (101305ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, pain from a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Adults: take 300 to 1000 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Up to 8 tablets (4000 mg) may be given in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severely reduced heart function; if you have had asthma caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have taken barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants; or if you have taken alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver impairment, kidney impairment, peptic ulcer, a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Do not take this medicine together with another anti-inflammatory analgesic, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have taken warfarin, lithium or a thiazide diuretic.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Fever and pain from a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain

groups.title: Tablet (D12500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening, and severe symptoms such as burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (257100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for paroxysmal pain of gastrointestinal disease and for functional disturbance and spasmodic pain of the biliary system, the urinary system and the female reproductive system, including dysmenorrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Do not exceed a maximum of 6 tablets in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity to it (rash, red spots, itching, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips); if you have had asthma caused by another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic; if you have severe kidney impairment or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; if you have glaucoma; if you have difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia; if you have functional narrowing of the gastrointestinal tract such as pyloric stenosis; if you have paralytic or obstructive intestinal obstruction; if you have severe muscle weakness or megacolon; if you have rapid heartbeat or tachyarrhythmia; if you have severe liver impairment, severe heart disease, haemorrhagic colitis, peptic ulcer or a severe blood disorder; or if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have bacterial diarrhoea; if you have or have had liver impairment; if you have Gilbert's syndrome (Meulengracht's disease); if you have impaired heart function (coronary insufficiency, heart failure, arrhythmia and the like); if you have or have had kidney impairment; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have bronchial asthma, ulcerative colitis, an overactive thyroid or fever; if you have prostatic hyperplasia; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are at risk of narrow-angle glaucoma; if you are prone to obstruction of the bowel or of the outlet of the ureter; or if you are prone to tachyarrhythmia.

Disturbance of eye accommodation may occur, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

People who have taken other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol must not take this medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium, a thiazide diuretic, a tetracyclic antidepressant, an antihistamine, an antipsychotic, quinidine, amantadine, disopyramide or another anticholinergic medicine (tiotropium, ipratropium, atropine-like compounds), an antidopaminergic medicine such as metoclopramide, a beta agonist, propantheline, chloramphenicol, probenecid, zidovudine, cholestyramine or flucloxacillin.

If thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, cyanosis, leukopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), flushing, skin reactions, abnormal sweating, itching, dry skin, urticaria, red spots, a fall in blood pressure including shock, anaphylactic shock, drug eruption, difficulty breathing, hypersensitivity, angioedema, rash, swelling (of the throat, eyelids, lips and the like), chest tightness, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, breathlessness, burn-like blisters, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), palpitations, rapid heartbeat, vertigo, fatigue, bronchospasm, thirst, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, abdominal distension, raised transaminases, difficulty passing urine, urinary retention, dilated pupils, ciliary muscle paralysis, disturbance of accommodation (in people with severe long-sightedness), anxiety, excitement, hallucination, headache, a heavy head or abnormally high body temperature occurs, or if unexpected abdominal pain continues or worsens, or occurs with fever, nausea, vomiting, a change in bowel movement, abdominal tenderness, a fall in blood pressure, fainting or bloody stools, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (A55700ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the heavy head, reflux, rough skin, boils, loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 3 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day, before bedtime (or on an empty stomach). For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the frequency and condition of bowel movements.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4; or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another laxative.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea or vomiting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (130501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and itching of the skin, and, in combination with a topical hydrocortisone preparation, for eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 6 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg), 1 time in 1 day, before bedtime; for people sensitive to adverse reactions, take 1/2 tablet (5 mg) per dose in the morning and in the evening as divided doses. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. In people with kidney impairment the dosing interval must be adjusted to kidney function, and in children with kidney impairment the dose must be adjusted individually according to renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if the user is a young child under 6 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia and the like); if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or about fertility.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, ritonavir or a large amount of alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drowsiness, headache; occasionally lassitude, numbness, weakness, agitation or abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary listlessness, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, movement disorder, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, loss of memory, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation or nightmares; occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, inflammation of the lips, taste disturbance or increased appetite; rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia or raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations or vasculitis; occasionally reduced white blood cells, reduced neutrophils, increased lymphocytes or increased eosinophils; rarely increased monocytes, increased or reduced platelets, or photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching or rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of eye accommodation, oculogyric crisis or vertigo; occasionally liver function disturbance such as raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, raised BUN, sugar in the urine or blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting or urinary retention; joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance or visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain.

Itching, urticaria and the like may appear after this medicine is stopped.

groups.title: Capsule (A52600ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for diarrhoea, diarrhoea with abdominal pain, indigestion, loose stools and vomiting with diarrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a newborn baby or a child aged 7 years or younger; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child; if you are an older person; if you have hypersensitivity to medicines; if you have diarrhoea with fever, or continuing bloody or mucous stools; or if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not take it for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with a gastrointestinal analgesic or an antispasmodic. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash, itching or, rarely, dry mouth occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (172806ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day; up to 3200 mg may be taken in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis: take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Ages 11 to 14 years: take 200 to 250 mg per dose. Ages 7 to 10 years: take 150 to 200 mg per dose. Ages 3 to 6 years: take 100 to 150 mg per dose. Ages 1 to 2 years: take 50 to 100 mg per dose. Take these doses by mouth 3 to 4 times in 1 day. A child weighing less than 30 kg must not be given more than 500 mg in 1 day, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Do not take more than the recommended dose.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are taking high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, or liver impairment now or in the past; if you have kidney impairment now or in the past; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease or high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, low-dose aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious cardiovascular adverse reactions may occur.

Taking this medicine may cause serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulceration and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor or low-dose aspirin.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure or heart failure; Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency; reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk. (Avoid drinking milk or taking an antacid within 1 hour after taking this medicine.)

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D14400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF) or Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not give it to a child under 2 years of age; if it is really necessary, see a doctor. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or if you are being given another medicine such as a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA), signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening, and severe symptoms such as burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
